properties.description:
ESFMSO

What: Widespread moderate rainfall over a prolonged period of time.
Storm total amounts between 1 to 3 inches for valleys and 2 to 3
inches for the mountains.  There is a 10 percent chance of isolated
rainfall amounts up to 4 inches along the Continental Divide.

Where: Flathead and Lake Counties in northwest Montana, including
Glacier National Park. Missoula county in west-central Montana.

Timing: Beginning Sunday morning, continuing through Monday night.
Heaviest rainfall rates anticipated Monday into Monday night.

Significant rainfall totals will bring potential for rapid rises on
streams and creeks, rock and debris slides and runoff issues in poor
drainage areas. Those recreating in the backcountry should take
caution on backcountry roadways for falling debris.

properties.description:
ESFTFX

Periods of rain are expected to begin on Sunday along the Rocky
Mountain Front and then spread eastward out over the plains of North
Central MT by Sunday night.

Overall, total rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches will be common over
North Central MT from Sunday through Monday, including the east side
of Glacier Park. There is a 10 percent chance of isolated rainfall
amounts up to 4 inches.

At this time no significant flooding is expected. However, in areas
that do receive closer to 3 inches or more of rainfall, some minor
field or small stream flooding can not be ruled out. Additionally,
some rocks could wash down on to roadways near mountains.

Those planning outdoor activities over the next few days should be
prepared for periods of rain.

properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Central
Interior-Dalton Highway Summits-Eielson AFB and Salcha-Two
Rivers-Upper Chena River Valley-White Mountains and High Terrain
South of the Yukon River-Upper Koyukuk Valley-Middle Yukon
Valley-Nenana-Chatanika River Valley-Fairbanks Metro Area

24 Hour rainfall totals across portions of the Western and Central
Interior have generally been between 0.75 and 1.25 inches due to
widespread moderate rainfall. This is a direct result of an
atmospheric river which continues to focus higher than normal levels
of moisture across the region.

Additional rainfall of .50 to as much as 1.50" inches will be
possible Friday evening through Saturday afternoon as a disturbance
aloft moves through and further interacts with the available
atmospheric moisture. Should this occur, 48 hours rainfall will
coincide with 5 to 10 year return intervals with locations receiving
the heaviest rainfall closer to 25 year return intervals.

While main stem rivers will be able to handle this extra volume of
water, some of the smaller feeder streams and rivers could see near
bankfull to minor flooding conditions. In addition increased stream
flows are expected for the next few days, so anyone planning
recreation activities on or along these waterways should exercise
extreme caution and be on the lookout for rapidly rising water
levels.
